T1158.long: To prevent normal users from accidentally changing special files on a system, most operating systems have the concept of a ‘hidden’ file. These files don’t show up when a user browses the file system with a GUI or when using normal commands on the command line. Users must explicitly ask to show the hidden files either via a series of Graphical User Interface (GUI) prompts or with command line switches (dir /a for Windows and ls –a for Linux and macOS).

strings: Kramatorsk, UN Compound conference room, vul.
Updates on Intersectorial networking and humanitarian planning 2020 and Monitoring framework updates.
Consultations with partners on GBV services monitoring in terms of accountability to affected population.
1. Updates in GBV SC joint action plan 2019.
Partners shared the updates on actual and upcoming GBV related activities in 2019.
campaign in forms of smart-parties for youth, events for children on sexual violence prevention.
is working on a range of available services, incl. specialized services for GBV survivors.
Child Protection Services of Donetsk Region State Administration. Algorithm for domestic violence mitigation and response is being elaborated. Planned participation in
by working with education facilities and local authorities, distributing information materials.
A need in study on how to respond to DV in case if child is a perpetrator was stressed, as well as to reveal the root causes of increasing perpetrating violence among men.
. Three mobile teams continue operating in conflict-affected areas, including
providing psychosocial support to population. Trainings for police officers, local authorities, educators on community resilience and providing PSS support for those in hardships are being conducted.
Donetsk Regional Social Center for Mother and Child. Maintain social, psychosocial and legal aid for women (mothers with toddlers) survived from violence.

Donetsk Regional Center of Psychosocial Support. Provide PSS support and primary legal aid, restoring of documents for those in hardships for the period up to three months. There is a lack of personnel to meet the need of elderly people and people with disabilities.
Centre for Social Support of ATO Veterans and their Families
campaign and also campaigns against bullying at schools. Planned trainings on conflict management and family resilience promotion. Providing coordination meeting jointly with IMC.

Kramatorsk Local Center for Free Secondary Legal Aid. Centers providing full cycle of legal aid for all social categories, including GBV survivors, cover (directly or via Free legal aid bureaus) majority of rayons along the
. Planned ad hoc awareness raising events (seminars, round tables, discussions) for both service providers and community members.

UN Women. Three project in Eastern Ukraine are carrying out, including GBV prevention component implemented jointly with UFPH. Among the upcoming events are: trainings for amalgamated communities in Donetsk, Luhansk, and Zaporizhzhia regions; round tables in 15 communities on safe cities working groups establishment. Working with Police on establishing the procedures and providing trainings for officers. One or two upcoming training expected this autumn in Mariupol and/or Kramatorsk.
ADRA. Trained mobile teams provide primary psychosocial support and referral information for GBV survivors. Planned activities within
campaign for children on nonviolent communication and behavior. Need: a lack of GBV data, including prevalence study.

. Implementing a project of MdM to address the needs of most vulnerable women and girls (subjected to substantial abuse, HIV-infected etc.) by providing them relevant humanitarian assistance. Currently are conducting a research on availability of sexual and reproductive health services for these categories. The study includes a set of violence related questions. Need: a lack and

or unavailability of safe spaces for women and girls living with HIV, sex workers and substances users. Due to such circumstances, these survivors often prevent themselves to seek any survivor-oriented services, deteriorating their life conditions.
. Currently are conducting a quantitative part of research on violence among vulnerable social groups. Plan conducting focus group discussions.
. Continue providing referral services, primary legal aid, hot-line (non-specialized for GBV, however providing referral information).

. A lack of comprehensive work with families is among key reasons of insufficient response to and mitigation the violence at early stages. Need: introducing education on sexual and reproductive health and rights (with focus on children and adolescents) may positively influence the risks of sexual assaults against them.
GBV SC team to share link to updated referral directory of available GBV services.
to provide GBV SC team with updated contacts of supported services to be further updated in the referral directory and disseminated among all GBV SC partners.
GBV SC team: to provide partners with a review of secondary data of existing GBV studies in Ukraine.
2. Updates on Intersectoral networking and humanitarian planning 2020 and Monitoring framework updates.

The partners were reminded about key prioritization criteria and groups of people with specific needs in the Ukrainian humanitarian response. In view of that, humanitarian GBV response should consider:
The necessity of multisectoral response due to multisectoral needs of affected population.
Key prioritization criteria: life-saving priority, geographical priority with taking into account specificity of protection issues, and vulnerability priority.
Needs of different groups: IDPs, residing on NGCA, people with disabilities and injuries, different gender with age groups, single headed households.
More sound data for evidence-based needs estimations and response planning.
The partners outlined key protection concerns that may expose GBV risks for affected population:

Although the conflict is suspended and not in an active phase, there are still concerns related to ensuring the access to justice for those living in settlements along the contact line. Despite the decreasing number of violence cases, we have a concern that it is underreported (Proliska).
A lack of reliable GBV data (several partners).
Need in complex PSS  support for service providers, especially educators who are faced with burnout and conflict related pressure. (ADRA).

Some parent has low awareness and sensitivity to issues related to violence and its manifestations and tend to justify acts of violence against children as an educational activity (Child Smile, Slavic Heart).
Awareness raising for police officers to boost understanding of GBV and DV issues and mitigation and response.

The partners were briefed on updated monitoring quarterly framework that includes data disaggregation for beneficiaries by gender with age, disability, residing on NGCA. Providing these disaggregation will allow to coordinate efforts of humanitarian actors while providing response for different groups and to adjust activities in accordance with specific needs.
GBV SC partners to provide disaggregated data by gender with age, disabilities, residing on NGCA.
GBV SC team to consolidate humanitarian needs updates provided by partners.
3. Consultations with partners on GBV services monitoring in terms of accountability to affected population

Accountability to affected population was declared as one of mandatory requirements in HPC 2019 process. Considering that, consultations with partners on possible methodologies to provide these estimations were conducted. Among possible effective methods the partners considered the following:
Anonymous online questionnaires that would be applicable for younger audience residing in cities.
Questionnaires aimed at assessing accessibility and availability of services and satisfaction rate.
Maintain regular feedback from clients in order to monitor satisfaction level and consider recommendations.
Deploy the corresponding questions to existing referral forms.
Specific needs, especially among most vulnerable categories, can be revealed due to focus group discussion.
GBV SC partners to suggest potential effective methods to implement accountability to affected population.
GBV SC team to consolidate the suggested inputs.
UNFPA launched medical mobile teams in Popasna, Bakhmut and Volnovakha raions.
UNFPA to share with partners contacts of mobile teams and working schedule.
